what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 4 of 4: Growth and drag against attraction: the dilute-gas condition, derived. SETTING (blocks 44-47; open PRs titled 'ail44: records with inertia', 'ail45: the wind law', 'ail46: the potential of the wind', 'ail47: transparent bodies'): a supplied clause, not adopted: a record's content is its direction of travel (sphere menu: a record with unit vector s steps to x + e_k with probability max(0, s.e_k)/sqrt 3; an occupied target exchanges contents; bonds re-draw their pair of contents uniformly on the momentum class at rate gamma); bodies are sets of solid sites that CAPTURE the records stepping onto them. ESTABLISHED: number and momentum conserved locally; uniform stationary measure; pressure rho/(3 sqrt 3), wave speed sqrt(1 - rho)/3; a body capturing Q per tick draws the wind g = sqrt3 Q/(4 pi r^2 (1 - rho)) (executed to 1-3 per cent), the wind of several bodies is the superposition of their potential flows (executed: fit coefficient 0.983-0.998, residual = noise); two capturing bodies attract with F = K Q1 Q2/r^2, K -> K_0 = sqrt3/(4 pi rho (1 - rho)) at low density and for dilute bodies; a capturing site takes up q_1 = (sqrt 3/2) rho per tick (executed 0.236-0.241 against 0.251 at rho = 0.29) and a body captures through its exposed faces; for bodies TRANSPARENT to the gas the force is G N1 N2/r^2 with G = 3 sqrt3 rho/(16 pi (1 - rho)) (executed at separation 16, rho = 0.3, gamma = 1: F/(N1 N2) = (1.44 +- 0.10)e-4 against 1.46e-4). COSTS, not yet executed: the same rate q_1 makes bodies grow and drags their motion towards the local wind; the supervisor's estimate is that attraction outruns both only when the gas inside an orbit weighs much less than the central body, about (4 pi/3) rho r^3 << N/6. TASK: (a) For a free transparent body of N capturing sites with momentum P (the sum of the contents it has captured) in the wind of another body, derive the equations of motion in the free-streaming regime: dN/dt = q_1 N, dP/dt = q_1 N <s>_wind(x) (captured records carry the wind's mean momentum), hence for the momentum per record p = P/N: dp/dt = q_1 (<s>_wind - p). State what velocity corresponds to p for a body (decide and justify: a body is a lump of records; how does it move?). (b) With <s>_wind = sqrt3 Q_1/(4 pi r^2 rho (1 - rho)) and Q_1 = q_1 N_1, find the time to fall from rest through a distance r and compare it with the growth-and-drag time 1/q_1: derive the condition under which a bound orbit survives many periods, with its numerical coefficient, and compare with the supervisor's estimate (4 pi/3) rho r^3 << N_1/6. (c) Say what happens to a two-body system over times long compared with 1/q_1 (the bodies are entrained by each other's wind: terminal relative velocity = wind speed). (d) Give the mass growth law and its consequence for the force over time. check.py: integrate the derived equations numerically for one case and check conservation bookkeeping exactly where possible.
